messages:
emily: deploy-bot flagged the py/ts SDK canary publish as FAILED :warning: signer mismatch on 0.37.0-canary. Blocking final release. logs: https://ci.redwood.ai/teams/devex/builds/9876

ben: ugh. what's the exact error from the signing step?

emily: paste of the log: ```ERROR: artifact signature validation failed
expected: 0xA1B2C3D4E5F6
found:    0x9F8E7D6C5B4A
package: redwood-sdk-0.37.0-canary-py3-none-any.whl```

carla: quick options: 1) rebuild+re-sign and republish a new canary build (preferable), 2) yank the canary and keep stable traffic, or 3) increment build metadata (0.37.0+ci1) and publish signed artifact.

carla: example republish steps we should run in CI (one-offs):
```bash
python -m build && gpg --detach-sign -a dist/*.whl && twine upload dist/* --skip-existing
# or for npm
npm version prerelease --preid=canary && npm publish --tag canary
```

ben: if we republish, we need to ensure consumers on Dedicated/Docker pulls pick the new tag. Also need to update the canary CV to not route traffic to the bad artifact.

danny: rollback criteria question: do we treat this as a hard rollback (revert canary) if >100 unique canary installs in the last 3 hours, or do we hold based on error-rate spike? we should codify.

alicia: agree we need a clear threshold. Suggest: if >100 active installs OR >1% of production token usage impacted then block final publish and trigger coordinated rollback. I've added a short doc to the release playbook — https://docs.redwood.ai/release/playbooks/sdk-canary-criteria

emily: plan: hold final publish for now, mark canary as yanked, spin a republish job with incremented build metadata (0.37.0+1) and CI signing key. I've opened a draft PR for release notes and rollback steps: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/3412 (WIP)

release-bot: canary hold placed by @emily — traffic routed to stable 0.36.2, canary tag frozen. :robot_face:

carla: small ops note — if CI uses ephemeral signing keys, double-check KMS policy for the runner. We had a similar issue in 2023 where the CI runner pulled an old key.

ben: can we also pin package resolution for the internal monorepo? add a temporary resolution in root package.json to force 0.36.2 for critical services while this is triaged. Example: "resolutions": { "@redwood/sdk": "0.36.2" }

danny: I'll update the rollback checklist in the ops repo: add steps for yank/unpublish, republish with +meta, and a traffic re-route playbook. Also include a short command snippet to unroll canary in k8s: `kubectl set image deployment/sdk-worker sdk-worker=redwood/sdk:0.36.2`

alicia: release notes: add a short note about the signer mismatch under Known Issues and the fix plan. Also include guidance for Dedicated customers to pin to 0.36.2 if they see issues. I'll draft the snippet for the docs.

emily: action items
- emily: escalate CI signing key and trigger republish job (now)
- carla: verify KMS runner policy and confirm key fingerprint (ETA 30m)
- ben: add package resolution to monorepo and notify platform teams (ETA 15m)
- danny: update rollback checklist and runbook (ETA 1h)
- alicia: draft release notes / Known Issues blurb and link in the PR (ETA 30m)

carla: once republish succeeds, we'll unfreeze canary and run smoke tests (smoke matrix listed in the PR). If any smoke test fails, immediate rollback to 0.36.2 and abort final publish. :thumbsup:

emily: thanks — I'll post an update in this thread when the republish job completes.

release-bot: deploy job 9877 queued by @emily — will report status here.
